kurals.tr: Sirumai Namakkozhiyach Chetchendraar Ulli / Narumalar Naanina Kan
kurals.m: While we endure the unbearable sorrow, your eyes weep for him who is gone afar, and shun (the sight of) fragrant flowers

kurals.tr: Nayandhavar Nalkaamai Solluva Polum / Pasandhu Panivaarum Kan
kurals.m: The discoloured eyes that shed tears profusely seem to betray the unkindness of our beloved

kurals.tr: Thanandhamai Saala Arivippa Polum / Manandhanaal Veengiya Thol
kurals.m: The shoulders that swelled on the day of our union (now) seem to announce our separation clearly (to the public)

kurals.tr: Panaineengip Paindhoti Sorum Thunaineengith / Tholkavin Vaatiya Thol
kurals.m: In the absence of your consort, your shoulders having lost their former beauty and fulness, your bracelets of pure gold have become loose

kurals.tr: Kotiyaar Kotumai Uraikkum Thotiyotu / Tholkavin Vaatiya Thol
kurals.m: The (loosened) bracelets, and the shoulders from which the old beauty has faded, relate the cruelty of the pitiless one

kurals.tr: Thotiyotu Tholnekizha Noval Avaraik / Kotiyar Enakkooral Nondhu
kurals.m: I am greatly pained to hear you call him a cruel man, just because your shoulders are reduced and your bracelets loosened

kurals.tr: Paatu Perudhiyo Nenje Kotiyaarkken / Vaatudhot Poosal Uraiththu
kurals.m: Can you O my soul! gain glory by relating to the (so-called) cruel one the clamour of my fading shoulders?

kurals.tr: Muyangiya Kaikalai Ookkap Pasandhadhu / Paindhotip Pedhai Nudhal
kurals.m: When I once loosened the arms that were in embrace, the forehead of the gold-braceleted women turned sallow

kurals.tr: Muyakkitaith Thanvali Pozhap Pasapputra / Pedhai Perumazhaik Kan
kurals.m: When but a breath of breeze penetrated our embrace, her large cool eyes became sallow

kurals.tr: Kannin Pasappo Paruvaral Eydhindre / Onnudhal Seydhadhu Kantu
kurals.m: Was it at the sight of what the bright forehead had done that the sallowness of her eyes became sad?
